report.executive_summary: Goldman Sachs (GS) reported a substantial financial recovery in 2024, reversing the decline seen in 2023. Consolidated net earnings increased by 67.64% to $14.28 billion, and diluted EPS rose by 77.26% to $40.54. This improvement was driven by a 16% increase in consolidated net revenues to $53.51 billion, fueled by strong performance in Global Banking & Markets and Asset & Wealth Management. Concurrently, the company resolved several significant legal contingencies, including a $65 million CFPB settlement and the dismissal of the 1MDB DPA, while restructuring its capital base through the redemption of $2.2 billion in preferred stock and the issuance of Series Z preferred stock. The 2024 filing reflects a strategic narrowing of consumer-focused operations, specifically the exit from GreenSky, and introduces new risk disclosures regarding geopolitical tariffs, AI technologies, and regulatory capital constraints, alongside a significant reduction in granular financial and legal narrative disclosures compared to 2023.
report.longitudinal_analysis: Between 2023 and 2024, Goldman Sachs underwent significant changes in disclosure scope and content. In 2023, disclosures included specific segment-level operating expenses for Global Banking & Markets, detailed Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) rollforward tables, and granular narratives on diversity metrics and private fund adviser rule implementation. The 2024 filing replaced segment-specific expense data with consolidated firm-wide operating expenses ($33.77 billion) and removed several specific financial tables, including the ACL rollforward and net interest income volume/rate variance analysis, indicating a shift towards less granular forward-looking commentary or completed status of certain risk exposures. Legally, the 2023 disclosure featured ongoing CFPB cooperation and active 1MDB DPA obligations, which were resolved in 2024 through a $65 million settlement and DPA dismissal, respectively. Conversely, legal risk re-emerged in 2024 with the appellate reversal of a dismissal in the Sea Limited litigation and a new settlement in principle. Structurally, 2024 introduced the Capital Solutions Group and the Platform Solutions segment, while removing specific references to the divested Personal Financial Management (PFM) business and the GreenSky partnership. Risk disclosure depth expanded in 2024, with geopolitical risks split into eight distinct categories including specific cyber attack and settlement failure consequences, and Artificial Intelligence elevated to a primary competitive and operational risk category with detailed technical and legal risk factors.
report.financial_analysis: Based on the supplied financial metrics and trends, Goldman Sachs demonstrated significant earnings growth between 2023 and 2024. Net Income Attributable to Parent increased from $8.52 billion in 2023 to $14.28 billion in 2024, a growth of 67.64%. Consequently, Diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS) rose from $22.87 to $40.54, representing a 77.26% increase. This EPS growth was supported by a reduction in the weighted average number of diluted shares outstanding, which decreased from 345.8 million in 2023 to 333.6 million in 2024 (-3.53%). In terms of balance sheet metrics, Total Assets grew modestly from $1,641.59 billion in 2023 to $1,675.97 billion in 2024 (2.09% growth). Total Stockholders' Equity increased from $116.91 billion to $122.00 billion (4.35% growth). Combined Debt decreased slightly from $317.82 billion to $312.34 billion (-1.72%). Consequently, the Debt-to-Equity ratio improved from 2.72x in 2023 to 2.56x in 2024. Operating cash flow remained negative in both years, worsening slightly from -$12.59 billion in 2023 to -$13.21 billion in 2024, resulting in an Operating Cash Flow to Net Income ratio shifting from -1.48x to -0.93x, indicating that while operating cash outflows persisted, the underlying profitability increased. Capital expenditures (Payments to Acquire PP&E) continued a declining trend, falling from $2.32 billion in 2023 to $2.09 billion in 2024 (-9.72%). Note that net revenues of $53.51 billion and $46.25 billion for 2024 and 2023 respectively are cited in the findings but were not part of the selected financial metrics used for the longitudinal calculations above.
limitations: The longitudinal financial analysis is limited to the specific metrics provided in the financial_data_notes and selected financial_metrics list. Broader revenue figures mentioned in the batch findings (e.g., $53.51 billion in 2024) were not included in the metric extraction list and therefore could not be used in the calculated trends. The analysis does not infer causes for financial changes beyond what is explicitly stated in the findings. Certain balance sheet and income statement details were removed from the 2024 disclosure, limiting the ability to perform granular segment or line-item variance analysis based on the provided data.

key_findings.title: Resolution of CFPB Investigation with $65M Settlement
key_findings.analysis: The disclosure changed from an ongoing cooperation with the CFPB in 2023 to a finalized resolution in 2024. GS Bank USA entered a consent order to pay a $45 million penalty and provide approximately $20 million in restitution, totaling $65 million, which has been fully paid. This transforms an open legal contingency into a definitive financial loss and legal conclusion.

key_findings.title: Reversal of Dismissal and Settlement in Sea Limited Litigation
key_findings.analysis: Legal proceedings regarding Sea Limited's 2021 offerings shifted from a favorable dismissal with prejudice in 2023 to an appellate reversal and a subsequent settlement in principle in 2024. While the settlement excludes GS Asia from contribution, the reversal of the dismissal resurrects legal risk and uncertainty that was previously resolved, altering the posture of the litigation.

key_findings.title: Formation of Capital Solutions Group
key_findings.analysis: A new organizational unit, the Capital Solutions Group, was formed in January 2025 within Global Banking & Markets. This new entity combines financing, origination, and risk management capabilities to expand coverage to financial sponsors and alternative asset managers, representing a structural change in the company's business model and strategic focus that was not present in the 2023 filing.

key_findings.title: Redemption of $2.2 Billion in Preferred Stock
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing discloses the redemption of all outstanding shares of Series K and Series P Preferred Stock, totaling $2.2 billion in redemption value. This action permanently retires these instruments, altering the equity structure. A $34 million difference between redemption value and net carrying value was recorded as an addition to preferred stock dividends.

key_findings.title: Shift from Segment to Consolidated Operating Expenses
key_findings.analysis: The disclosure of operating expenses shifted from a segment-level figure for Global Banking & Markets ($18.04 billion in 2023) to the firm's consolidated total ($33.77 billion in 2024). This change in scope from divisional to enterprise-wide represents a fundamental shift in the magnitude and transparency of the reported financial metric.

key_findings.title: Granular Disclosure of Geopolitical and Cyber Risks
key_findings.analysis: The 2023 disclosure regarding geopolitical risks (Russia-Ukraine, Middle East, US-China, China-Taiwan) was split into eight distinct disclosures in 2024. This change allowed for more granular identification of specific risks, including the addition of 'cyber attacks' and 'settlement failures' as potential consequences of conflict escalation, highlighting increased operational and financial exposures.

key_findings.title: Removal of Key Financial and Legal Disclosures
key_findings.analysis: Several material disclosures present in 2023 were removed in 2024. These include specific balance sheet figures for collateralized financings (Resale agreements, Securities borrowed/loaned), the Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) rollforward table, and the net interest income volume/rate variance analysis. Additionally, the disclosure of the $215 million employment discrimination class action settlement was removed, indicating its final execution and release of associated legal reserves.

key_findings.title: Significant Reversal in Financial Performance (Earnings and Revenue Growth)
key_findings.analysis: Goldman Sachs reported a substantial improvement in financial performance for 2024 compared to 2023. Net earnings increased from $8.52 billion to $14.28 billion, and diluted EPS rose from $22.87 to $40.54. Concurrently, consolidated net revenues grew 16% to $53.51 billion, reversing the 2% decline seen in 2023. This positive trend was driven by higher revenues in net interest income, investment banking, and other principal transactions.

key_findings.title: Shift in Principal Transactions Drivers and Strategy
key_findings.analysis: The composition of 'other principal transactions' revenues changed significantly. In 2023, growth was primarily driven by derivatives related to borrowings. By 2024, the $4.65 billion revenue (a 119% increase) was driven by private equity investments, derivatives related to funding activities, and the impact of the Marcus loan portfolio sale. This indicates a strategic shift in how the firm generates gains from principal transactions.

key_findings.title: Strategic Narrowing of Platform Solutions and GreenSky Exit
key_findings.analysis: The firm explicitly stated it is narrowing its focus on consumer-related activities within the Platform Solutions segment. While 2023 disclosures highlighted point-of-sale financing via GreenSky, the 2024 filing omits this specific partnership from the consumer platforms description, focusing instead on credit cards (Apple Card) and transaction banking. This aligns with the reported 3% headcount increase in Asset & Wealth Management, partially offset by the sale of GreenSky.

key_findings.title: Key Executive Leadership Changes
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure shows a departure in senior leadership compared to 2023. Specifically, disclosures regarding Mr. Berlinski (Global Treasurer/CEO of GS Bank USA) and Mr. Lee (Chief Risk Officer) are removed from the 2024 executive officer list. This represents a material change in the company's governance and operational leadership structure.

key_findings.title: New Capital Raise: Series Z Preferred Stock
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing discloses a new capital raising event occurring in January 2025, the issuance of 76,000 shares of Series Z 6.85% Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock. This introduces a new equity instrument with specific dividend and redemption terms, expanding the company's capital base.

key_findings.title: Removal of Specific Strategic and Credit Risk Disclosures
key_findings.analysis: Several specific disclosures present in the 2023 filing were removed or obscured in 2024. The explicit confirmation of the 2023 divestiture of the Personal Financial Management (PFM) business is no longer stated, replaced by broader 'narrowing focus' language. Additionally, the specific methodology change for assessing U.S. residential mortgage loan credit quality (using FICO/LTV instead of internal ratings) and its quantified impact were removed, altering the transparency of credit risk assessment details.

key_findings.title: Legal Risk Landscape Shift: Litigation Resolutions and Removed Narratives
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure reflects a significant reduction in specific legal contingencies compared to 2023. Three distinct legal proceedings previously detailed were removed: CDO-related securities litigation dismissed with prejudice in November 2023 (M0128), securities lending antitrust litigation where a preliminary settlement was approved in September 2023 with full reserves (M0137), and aluminum commodities litigation where the firm had already paid its settlement contribution (M0138). The removal of these items indicates resolved liabilities. Additionally, the 2024 filing removed the specific narrative regarding the $1.97 billion increase in the Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) in 2022, which cited macroeconomic concerns and industry-specific downgrades in TMT and real estate (M0100). This removal alters the disclosed historical risk drivers for that period, shifting from specific sectoral exposure narratives to potentially less granular forward-looking commentary.

key_findings.title: Escalation of Geopolitical and Regulatory Compliance Risks
key_findings.analysis: Goldman Sachs significantly expanded its risk disclosures in 2024 to reflect concrete political and regulatory developments. The company moved from general election uncertainty to specific references to the U.S. presidential election results and imposed tariffs on China, explicitly linking these to reduced investment banking revenues and transaction volumes (M0179). Furthermore, the disclosure of Federal Reserve Board (FRB) oversight constraints on capital distributions was newly introduced in 2024, warning that failure to comply with capital requirements or resubmit a capital plan may limit dividends and share repurchases without FRB approval (M0216). Regulatory risk regarding capital adequacy also escalated from a static description of the Stress Capital Buffer (SCB) to active litigation and imminent framework changes, noting a December 2024 lawsuit by trade groups (including GS) against the FRB and planned 2025 CCAR modifications (M0320).

key_findings.title: Deepening Focus on Artificial Intelligence and Technological Competition
key_findings.analysis: The treatment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) risks expanded materially between 2023 and 2024. The 2024 disclosure now details specific technical and legal risks, including generative AI output errors, bias, privacy breaches, IP infringement, and the evolving regulatory environment, noting that model complexity limits transparency and oversight (M0209). In the competitive landscape, AI was explicitly elevated to a primary driver of competitive pressure alongside distributed ledgers, with warnings that competitors' successful AI integration could reduce GS's market share and revenue through improved productivity and client offerings (M0236). This marks a shift from AI as a mention in existing technology risks to a standalone, high-priority operational and strategic risk category.

key_findings.title: Significant Financial Performance Improvement in 2024
key_findings.analysis: Net revenues increased 16% year-over-year to $53.51 billion in 2024, a sharp reversal from the 2% decrease to $46.25 billion in 2023. This growth was driven primarily by strong performance in Global Banking & Markets (specifically Equities, Investment Banking fees, and FICC) and Asset & Wealth Management (Equity investments and Management fees), whereas 2023 declines were led by lower FICC and Investment Banking fees (M0432). This quantifiable improvement suggests a recovery in trading and advisory activity compared to the prior year.

key_findings.title: Reversal of Investment Banking Revenue Trend and Driver Shift
key_findings.analysis: Investment banking revenues reversed a prior-year decline, increasing 24% to $7.74 billion in 2024 from $6.22 billion in 2023. The primary drivers shifted from lower M&A activity in 2023 to higher M&A activity and significant increases in debt and equity underwriting in 2024, signaling a recovery in the Global Banking segment.

key_findings.title: Shift in Commissions and Fees Performance Drivers
key_findings.analysis: The disclosure moved from attributing 2023 revenue variance to a specific prior-year distortion (GreenSky) to attributing 2024 growth to operational factors like higher Equities market volumes and transaction fees, offset by a loss from the GM credit card program transition. This represents a change in the substance of performance explanation.

key_findings.title: Reversal in Net Interest Income Direction and Drivers
key_findings.analysis: Net interest income reversed from a 17% decrease in 2023 to a 27% increase in 2024, reaching $8.06 billion. The drivers shifted from interest expense impacting expense offsets in 2023 to higher balances and rates impacting income in 2024, with new detail on collateralized financings and deposits.

key_findings.title: Change in Provision for Credit Losses Scope and Drivers
key_findings.analysis: The provision for credit losses scope shifted from segment-specific commercial real estate focus in 2023 ($401 million) to firm-wide drivers in 2024 ($1.35 billion), specifically credit card portfolio charge-offs and wholesale loan impairments, along with reserve reductions from portfolio transactions.

key_findings.title: Reversal in Operating Expense Drivers
key_findings.analysis: Operating expenses shifted from being driven by significant impairments and fees (increases) in 2023 to lower impairments (decreases) in 2024. This structural change in expense composition and direction meaningfully alters the understanding of cost performance.

key_findings.title: Significant Improvement in Asset & Wealth Management Performance
key_findings.analysis: Asset & Wealth Management reported a significant increase in pre-tax earnings from $1.36 billion in 2023 to $4.55 billion in 2024. This was driven by a 16% increase in net revenues and a 9% decrease in operating expenses due to lower commercial real estate CIE impairments.

key_findings.title: New Strategic Target for Credit Alternative Assets
key_findings.analysis: The company introduced a new strategic target to grow total credit alternative assets to $300 billion by the end of 2028, defining a clear future business priority and capital allocation strategy within the Asset & Wealth Management division.

key_findings.title: Updates to Subsidiary Capital and Funding Figures
key_findings.analysis: The disclosure updated financial figures for capital and funding provided by Group Inc. to regulated subsidiaries as of December 2024 compared to 2023, showing specific increases in equity investments for entities such as GS&Co. and GS Bank USA.

key_findings.title: Introduction of Platform Solutions Business Segment
key_findings.analysis: A new business segment, 'Platform Solutions,' was introduced, describing credit card issuance (Apple Card), deposits from Apple Card customers, and transaction banking services for corporate clients, representing a distinct new business line.

key_findings.title: Change in Allowance for Credit Losses Drivers
key_findings.analysis: The drivers of the allowance decrease shifted from specific portfolio sales (GreenSky, Marcus) in 2023 to an improved macroeconomic environment in the wholesale portfolio in 2024, indicating a change in fundamental credit risk exposure.

key_findings.title: Cessation of Unsecured Installment Loan Commitments
key_findings.analysis: In the third quarter of 2024, the company ceased providing commitments for unsecured installment loans, a line of consumer credit business it previously offered. This modification removes a specific product offering from its consumer credit portfolio, leaving only credit card lines as the described method of providing consumer credit.

key_findings.title: Dismissal of 1MDB-Related Deferred Prosecution Agreement
key_findings.analysis: The Deferred Prosecution Agreement (DPA) entered into with the U.S. Department of Justice regarding the 1MDB investigations was officially dismissed on May 6, 2024. This update resolves the final active legal obligation under the DPA, altering the firm's regulatory status compared to the 2023 disclosure which described the agreement as still active and pending expiration.

key_findings.title: Resolution of Oak Street Health Underwriting Litigation via Settlement
key_findings.analysis: In December 2024, the court approved a settlement for the securities class action related to Oak Street Health's offerings, which requires no financial contribution from the firm. This definitive resolution removes the uncertainty and potential liability associated with the pending class certification motion and trial risk noted in 2023.

key_findings.title: Removal of Diversity Goal Performance Metrics
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 disclosure removes the specific quantitative performance metrics against aspirational diversity goals (e.g., hires by gender and ethnicity, Vice President demographics) that were detailed in the 2023 filing. While goals are noted to expire in 2025, the removal of actual performance data eliminates key transparency regarding the company's progress on stated inclusion objectives.

key_findings.title: Removal of Private Fund Adviser Rule Implementation Disclosure
key_findings.analysis: The 2024 filing omits the detailed narrative regarding the implementation of SEC private fund adviser rules, including requirements for quarterly statements, annual audits, and fairness opinions, which was present in 2023. This removal suggests either the completion of the required system enhancements or a strategic shift in disclosing ongoing compliance burdens and operational risks related to these rules.

key_findings.title: Omission of Personal Financial Management (PFM) Business Sale
key_findings.analysis: The disclosure stating that the firm sold its Personal Financial Management (PFM) business during 2023 is absent in the 2024 filings. This removal indicates that the business line is fully divested and no longer part of the current operational or strategic discussion in the annual report.

key_findings.title: Removal of FDIC and Non-U.S. Insured Deposit Data
key_findings.analysis: Specific data points regarding FDIC-insured deposits ($221.52 billion as of December 2023) and non-U.S. insured deposits ($26.00 billion as of December 2023), along with the explanation of a January 2023 program change affecting eligibility, have been removed from the 2024 disclosure. This reduces transparency on liquidity stability and regulatory compliance exposure levels for insured deposits.

key_findings.title: Final Resolution of U.S. Treasury Securities Litigation
key_findings.analysis: The disclosure concerning U.S. Treasury securities market manipulation litigation, which was dismissed with prejudice and affirmed by the Second Circuit in 2024, has been removed from the 2024 filing. This signifies the matter is fully closed, eliminating any remaining legal uncertainty or potential appeal costs associated with this long-standing case.

key_findings.title: Introduction of Delayed Derivative Settlement Risk
key_findings.analysis: A new risk factor was introduced in 2024 highlighting that derivative contracts and secondary bank loans are not always confirmed or settled timely by counterparties. This introduces heightened credit and operational risks due to counterparty delays, a specific operational risk detail not explicitly present in the prior year's matched disclosures.

key_findings.title: Updated Timeline for General Motors Credit Card Program Transition
key_findings.analysis: The firm updated the status of its agreement with General Motors to transition its credit card program, specifying that the agreement was entered into in 2024 and completion is expected in the third quarter of 2025. This adds concrete temporal specificity to the strategic divestiture compared to the broader timeline provided in 2023.

sources.text: The FRB's Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review (CCAR) is designed to ensure that large BHCs, including us, have sufficient capital to permit continued operations during times of economic and financial stress.
As required by the FRB, we perform an annual capital stress test and incorporate the results into an annual capital plan, which we submit to the FRB for review.
Under the FRB's rule applicable to BHCs with $100 billion or more in total consolidated assets, including us, the SCB applies to the Standardized approach capital requirements.

The SCB reflects stressed losses estimated under the supervisory severely adverse scenario of the CCAR stress tests, as calculated by the FRB, and includes four quarters of planned common stock dividends.

The SCB, which is subject to a 2.5% floor, is generally effective on October 1 of each year and remains in effect until October 1 of the following year, unless it is reset in connection with the resubmission of a capital plan.

The SCB rule requires a BHC to receive the FRB's approval for any dividend, stock repurchase or other capital distribution, other than a capital distribution on a newly issued capital instrument, if the BHC is required to resubmit its capital plan, which may occur if the BHC determines there has been or will be a "material change" in its risk profile, financial condition or corporate structure since the plan was last submitted, or if the FRB directs the BHC to revise and resubmit its capital plan.
As part of the CCAR process, the FRB evaluates our plan to make capital distributions across a range of macroeconomic and company-specific assumptions, based on our and the FRB's own stress tests.

In December 2024 and February 2025, the FRB indicated that it intends to propose significant changes to the stress test framework in 2025 and, for the 2025 stress test, take steps to reduce the volatility of results and to begin to improve model transparency.
Also in December 2024, trade groups representing major U.S. banks, including us, filed a lawsuit against the FRB concerning certain inadequacies with its stress testing process.
